clue.text: Charlie's ban on banter, perhaps …

parts.note: the word 'ban' is the first half of the word 'banter', so it stands for half
banter is an example of wit, quick clever talk

explanation.surface: Someone called Charlie is said to have outlawed joking around.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: 'ban' is half of 'banter', and banter is a kind of wit, so 'ban' is HALF of WIT. The trailing dots lead into 5 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie is British slang for a fool, a simpleton with little sense.

clue.text: University out of time on brilliant poet

indicators.note: the university letter is taken out of the word for a time period

parts.note: an hour is a measure of time
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A student drops out of college after a period spent with a gifted writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a celebrated Roman lyric writer of odes and satires.

clue.text: Many, for example, feeding cat

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.definitionFit: Legion means a great number, as in 'their name is legion'.

clue.text: Plant is expected to hang initially within straggly bower

parts.note: will expresses what is expected to happen

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the scrambled word
straggly means untidy and sprawling, so the letters of bower are disordered
takes the first letter of hang

explanation.surface: A plant is supposed to droop down inside an overgrown arbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Willowherb, such as rosebay, is a wild flowering plant with willow-like leaves.

clue.text: Middle of body approximately below top in theory

indicators.note: in a down entry the later piece sits below the earlier one
in a down entry the top of a word is its opening letter

explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: … quite the opposite, as good man breaking oath of old

parts.note: egad is an old-fashioned mild oath
he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1 Across: the opposite is true, as a virtuous man breaks an antique vow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition depends on 1 Across: the opposite of a fool is a brainy person.
explanation.definitionFit: An intellectual is the opposite of a fool, so this follows on from the previous clue's dimwit.

clue.text: Lovely flower beds go — is cutting?

explanation.definitionFit: Exquisite means extremely beautiful and delicate.

clue.text: Sand in bottle

definitions.meaning: fine particles of stone or sand
British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.definitionFit: Grit is coarse sandy particles, and also pluck or determination.

clue.text: Villain or devil incarnate, ultimately infernal

clue.text: Neither won nor lost many — chose randomly

parts.note: a team that drew a match neither won nor lost
lots means many

explanation.definitionFit: Drawing lots means selecting by chance, picking at random.

clue.text: Splendid local offering sent back

parts.note: the local is the neighbourhood pub, and beer such as lager is what it offers

explanation.surface: A pint served at the neighbourhood pub is returned to the bar, despite being excellent.

explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly, hence magnificent or grand in appearance.

clue.text: Necessity is in recompense

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the synonym for recompense

parts.note: to requite is to repay or recompense

explanation.definitionFit: A requisite is something required, an essential item.

clue.text: One hooked on bars?

parts.note: suggests a drinker addicted to pubs, but the bars are bars of chocolate

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a pub addict or perhaps a gymnast on parallel bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone addicted to chocolate is hooked on chocolate bars.

clue.text: In Hyderabad, a legume?

explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'HyderabaD A Legume', and the whole clue also describes the answer, as dal is eaten in Hyderabad.

clue.text: Criminal snatches item, getting reprimand

clue.text: Opposition on the case, punch the air!

clue.text: Holding flag up, Australian natives found in honourable retirement

explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a professor retired with an honorary title kept.

the abbreviation is removed from the word magistrate

clue.text: Unfortunately, I'm too warty to impress old lover, a turn-off

clue.text: Finally, loveless princess put on right slipper?

clue.text: Narrative including header in equaliser, getting level

clue.text: Mock paper

definitions.meaning: to tease or make fun of someone
slang for a low-grade newspaper, a tabloid

explanation.definitionFit: To rag is to tease; a rag is a disreputable newspaper.

clue.text: Unsportingly unsporting?

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means unfair or dishonourable, against the spirit of fair play.

clue.text: Doctrine was concerned with love, no answer to it

parts.note: cared means was concerned
love is zero in tennis, O

clue.text: Elephants perhaps identified by the ears, they say?

parts.note: heard means picked up by the ears

explanation.definitionFit: Elephants live in groups, so a herd is an example of elephants together.
